references.text: Moses places the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece of Aaron during the consecration, fulfilling the command in Exodus 28:30.
Joshua shall stand before the priest Eleazar, who will seek counsel for him through the Urim judgment before the Lord's face.
Moses' blessing over the tribe of Levi mentions the Thummim and Urim as belonging to the Lord's faithful servant.
Saul asked the Lord, but the Lord did not answer him, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.
Certain individuals were excluded from priestly service until a priest could appear with the Urim and Thummim.
Parallel to Ezra 2:63 - some were excluded from priestly service until a priest could decide the matter with the Urim and Thummim.
The description of the breastpiece (hoshen) where the Urim and Thummim were to be placed, along with the twelve stones representing the tribes of Israel.
Aaron shall carry the names of the sons of Israel in the breastpiece over his heart when he enters the sanctuary, as a perpetual memorial before the Lord's face.
Christ, as high priest, enters the Most Holy Place once for all, fulfilling what Aaron did symbolically when he entered before the Lord's face.
Complementary descriptions of how Aaron carries Israel's children on his heart and shoulders as a reminder and judgment before the Lord's face.
A complementary function where the priest bears the people's guilt (p. 28:38) and judgment (p. 28:30) to secure favor with God.
The development from carrying the people's names as a memorial to actively confessing and transferring their sins on Yom Kippur.
